idiom_name: Pekko/Akka EventStream (publish/subscribe by event type, ActorRef subscribers)
implementation_notes: The aggregator is the actor system's event stream: ActorSystem.eventStream is a pub-sub stream whose channels are Classes and whose subscribers are ActorRefs, so subscribe(actorRef, classOf[OrderPlaced]) receives that type and any subtype while publish(event) delivers asynchronously into each subscriber's mailbox, and unsubscribe(actorRef) or terminating the actor ends the subscription. Because the stream is built on EventBus/SubchannelClassification, the type hierarchy itself is the channel tree - subscribing to a supertype widens the subscription - and the EventBus trait can be mixed in to build a differently classified bus (lookup, scanning, predicate or subchannel) with the same publish/subscribe surface. Outside an actor system, a small hand-written bus (a ConcurrentHashMap of callback lists, or a typed channel with ClassTag) is still justified, and the standard library ships no in-process event bus of its own.
code_sketch:
val stream = system.eventStream                 // one hub per ActorSystem

stream.subscribe(billing, classOf[OrderPlaced]) // channels are Classes; subtypes match too
stream.publish(OrderPlaced(id, total))          // asynchronous: one mailbox message each
stream.unsubscribe(billing)                     // or terminate the actor

// custom classification: mix in EventBus with Lookup/Subchannel classification
pitfalls: Subscriptions are by type hierarchy, so subscribing to Any or a broad supertype silently receives far more traffic than intended.
Delivery is asynchronous through mailboxes: publish returns immediately, ordering holds only per subscriber mailbox, and a busy subscriber's mailbox grows unbounded without a backpressure story.

The system event stream is shared with logging and actor-system events; high-rate domain traffic belongs on a dedicated EventBus instance rather than the system stream, otherwise logging configuration and domain events interfere.
Subscribers are ActorRefs held strongly by the stream, so short-lived subscribers must unsubscribe explicitly (or be terminated) or they stay reachable.
